- When sentiment is negative (avg < 0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 2–4% to avoid overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of true.  
- When sentiment is positive (avg > 0) and model forecasts are rising, check for horizon mismatch — 30d forecasts often overreact; reduce slope of forecast by 10–20% if sentiment is weakly positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.5% to catch early reversal.
